blocks.orig: Welcome to Tanzania! Upon your arrival at Dar es Salaam Airport, our friendly and knowledgeable guide will be eagerly waiting to warmly welcome you. He will be readily available to assist you and ensure a smooth transfer to your hotel. Sit back, relax, and let us take care of all your travel needs, providing you with a memorable and unforgettable experience in Tanzania.
blocks.html: Welcome to Tanzania! When you land at Dar es Salaam Airport, our friendly guide, who knows the country well, will be there waiting to greet you. He is on hand to help you and makes sure your transfer to the hotel goes smoothly. Lean back and relax while we look after everything you need for the journey, so your time in Tanzania becomes a memorable experience.

blocks.orig: Mikumi National Park lies at a six-hour drive from Dar Es Salaam and is Tanzania's fourth largest national park. The open horizons and abundant wildlife draw frequent comparisons to the more famous Serengeti plains, but its location close to Tanzania's largest city makes Mikumi easier accessible. The park has a great variety of animals: elephants, buffalos, zebras and giraffes are relatively easy to spot, as well as lions mating and many hippos in the resident hippo pool!
blocks.html: Six hours by road from Dar Es Salaam, you reach Mikumi National Park, the fourth largest national park in Tanzania. Its wide horizons and plentiful wildlife are often compared with the better-known Serengeti plains, yet because it sits near Tanzania's largest city, Mikumi is easier to get to. The range of animals is broad: you can spot elephants, buffalos, zebras and giraffes fairly easily, plus mating lions and plenty of hippos in the resident hippo pool!

blocks.orig: Udzungwa Mountains National Park is a relatively small, mountainous national park, known for its rare endemic species. In this tropical rainforest, you encounter bush elephants, monkeys, several smaller mammals, and over 400 bird species. Animals that can only be found here are primates such as the red Iringa Colobus and the Sanje Crested Mangabey. But also the grey-faced sengi (an elephant shrew) is endemic to Udzungwa as are several remarkable bird species.
blocks.html: Udzungwa Mountains National Park is fairly small and mountainous, and it is famous for rare endemic species. This tropical rainforest is home to bush elephants, monkeys, a number of smaller mammals and more than 400 bird species. Some primates live nowhere else, such as the red Iringa Colobus and the Sanje Crested Mangabey. The grey-faced sengi (an elephant shrew) is also endemic to Udzungwa, and so are a number of notable bird species.

blocks.orig: There are no paved roads in this national park, which means it’s perfect for shorter and longer hikes. The four-hour hike to the Sanje waterfalls is both challenging and refreshing, as you hike up the mountain but can reward yourself with a plunge at the bottom of the waterfall. Along the way, you might just spot one of those rare monkeys in the trees or see elephant tracks (of so-called mountain elephants). Keep in mind that it can be hot during midday, but if you stay in the shade and hydrated, this is a great walk!
blocks.html: With no paved roads inside the park, it is ideal for both short and long hikes. The four-hour walk to the Sanje waterfalls is tough as well as refreshing: you climb the mountain, and at the foot of the waterfall you can treat yourself to a swim. On the way you may see one of those rare monkeys in the trees, or come across elephant tracks (left by the so-called mountain elephants). Bear in mind that midday can be hot, but if you keep to the shade and drink enough, it is a lovely walk!

blocks.orig: Ruaha National Park is the third largest national park in Tanzania. It lies along the Great Ruaha River, is known for its large elephant population, and is a true paradise for birdwatchers with over 570 species. Besides, you might catch a glimpse of lions, leopards, giraffes, zebras, crocodiles, elands, sable antelopes, jackals, or the rare African wild dog. Game drives are special, as you drive through an untouched ecosystem in this relatively quiet but stunning park!
blocks.html: Tanzania's third largest national park is Ruaha National Park. Set along the Great Ruaha River, it is known for its big elephant population, and with more than 570 species it is a real haven for birdwatchers. You may also get to see lions, leopards, giraffes, zebras, crocodiles, elands, sable antelopes, jackals or the rare African wild dog. The game drives feel special, because you travel through an unspoilt ecosystem in a park that is fairly quiet yet beautiful!

blocks.orig: This is your last day! Today you fly to Julius Nyerere International Airport in Dar Es Salaam, from where you will catch your international flight home. Having second thoughts? Then don't hesitate to extend your holiday to one of Tanzania's paradise islands such as Zanzibar, Pemba, or Mafia!
blocks.html: Your final day has arrived! You fly today to Julius Nyerere International Airport in Dar Es Salaam, where your international flight home departs. Not ready to leave yet? Then feel free to add a few days on one of Tanzania's tropical islands such as Zanzibar, Pemba or Mafia!
